name: TCS NQT (Ninja, Digital, Prime)
tagline: One national test that routes you to TCS Ninja, Digital or Prime offers

overview.about: TCS hires most freshers through the TCS National Qualifier Test (NQT), delivered on TCS iON. A single test with a Foundation and an Advanced section decides which track you are considered for: Ninja (Foundation scores), or Digital and Prime (Advanced section, higher packages). Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.
eligibility: B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech/MCA/M.Sc from the batches named in the notification
Typically 60% or more in 10th, 12th/diploma and graduation (as reported; check current notice)
Active backlogs must be cleared before joining; education-gap limits apply as per notice
Register on TCS NextStep and apply for the NQT drive before the deadline

pattern.paper: Part A — Foundation: Numerical, Verbal, Reasoning
pattern.note: Clears you for Ninja; sections are individually timed
Hidden test cases; choose C/C++/Java/Python etc.
Technical + Managerial + HR, often one panel

overview.frequency: NQT cycles run several times a year; dates are announced on TCS NextStep

cards.title: One test, three outcomes
cards.body: You don't apply separately for Ninja and Digital any more. Everyone takes the NQT; your section scores decide whether you are interviewed for Ninja, Digital or Prime. Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.

cards.title: Foundation section
cards.body: Numerical ability, verbal ability and reasoning ability, each with its own timer. Easy-to-moderate questions from the aptitude syllabus. Strong Foundation scores alone can get a Ninja interview.

cards.title: Advanced section
cards.body: Advanced quantitative and reasoning MCQs plus an advanced coding section (2–3 problems, about 90 minutes). This is what makes you eligible for Digital and Prime.

cards.title: The three tracks
points: Digital: higher package, needs good Advanced + coding scores
Prime: highest fresher package, for top NQT performers
Packages change every year — read the offer details on the official page

cards.title: Timed sections
cards.body: Once a section's timer ends (or you submit it), you usually cannot return to it. Budget time per question and don't leave easy marks on the table.

cards.title: Strategy
cards.body: Aim to clear Foundation comfortably first, then push in the Advanced section. Solve at least one coding problem fully (all test cases) rather than two problems partially.

cards.q: Which part of the NQT makes you eligible for TCS Digital or Prime?
cards.explain: Digital and Prime are decided by Advanced-section performance, followed by interviews.

cards.q: Where do candidates register for the TCS NQT hiring process?
cards.explain: Use the official TCS NextStep portal; TCS never charges recruitment fees.

cards.title: Numerical style
cards.body: Short calculation questions: percentages, ratios, time-work, speed, P&C, probability, data interpretation tables. Expect 1–2 minutes each.

cards.title: Sample numerical
cards.body:
Q: A sum doubles in 5 years at simple interest. In how many years does it become 4 times?
SI for 5 years = P → rate 20%. To gain 3P you need 15 years.

cards.title: Verbal style
cards.body: Sentence completion, error spotting, reading comprehension, para-jumbles and word usage. Read each RC question before the passage.

cards.title: Reasoning style
cards.body: Number/letter series, coding-decoding, blood relations, seating arrangement, statement–assumption, data sufficiency and visual reasoning.

cards.title: Sample data sufficiency
cards.body:
Q: Is x even? (1) x² is even. (2) x is a multiple of 3.
(1) alone: x² even ⇒ x even (for integers) → sufficient. (2) alone: 3 or 6 → not sufficient. Answer: statement 1 alone.

cards.title: Sample advanced quant
cards.body:
Q: How many 3-digit numbers are divisible by 7?
First 105, last 994 → (994 − 105)/7 + 1 = 128.

cards.title: Practise on the real interface
cards.body: TCS iON tests use an on-screen interface with a timer per section. Take at least two full-length timed mocks before the test day.

cards.q: A sum doubles in 4 years at simple interest. The rate is:
How many 2-digit numbers are divisible by 6?
Is integer n odd? (1) n + 1 is even. (2) n² is odd. Which is sufficient?
cards.explain: Both (1) and (2) independently force n to be odd.

cards.title: Coding environment
cards.body: You read input from standard input and print to standard output. Hidden test cases check edge cases; output format must match exactly — no extra prompts like 'Enter n'.

cards.title: Typical easy problem
cards.body:
Print the sum of digits of each number in a list.
n = int(input())
for _ in range(n):
    x = input().strip().lstrip('-')
    print(sum(int(d) for d in x))

cards.title: Typical topics
points: Greedy and simple DP for Advanced coding

cards.title: Technical interview
cards.body: Expect: your final-year project in depth, one language (OOP), DBMS/SQL queries, OS basics, a small code on paper, and why you chose your stream.

cards.title: Managerial & HR
cards.body: Managerial checks situational judgement and attitude ('your teammate misses deadlines…'). HR covers relocation, shifts, documents and your interest in TCS.

cards.title: Read the problem twice
cards.body: Most failed test cases come from ignoring constraints (n up to 10⁵, negative numbers, empty input). Test with the sample and one edge case before submitting.

cards.q: In the TCS coding round, your program should:
options: Read from standard input and print only the required output
Read from a file named input.txt
cards.explain: Extra text breaks automated output matching.

cards.q: Which is most likely in a TCS technical interview for freshers?
options: Designing a distributed database from scratch
Only puzzles with no technical questions
Explaining your project and writing a small program
cards.explain: Fresher technical rounds focus on fundamentals and your own work.
